questions.title: Fibonacci Term by Recursion
questions.description:

    def fib(n):

questions.title: Fast Power by Halving
questions.description:
An offline calculator must raise base to the exponent e without looping: the fast-power (exponentiation by squaring) method halves the exponent recursively.

The program scaffolding (input reading and main) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def fast_power(base, e):

Compute base raised to the power e RECURSIVELY with the halving method: fast_power(base, 0) = 1; compute half = fast_power(base, e // 2); return half * half when e is even and half * half * base when e is odd. Loops are banned on this floor — the grader rejects any for/while keyword.

Input Format:
Line 1: two integers base and e separated by a space.

Output Format:
One line with base ** e.

Constraints:
1 <= base <= 10
0 <= e <= 18
questions.sourcecode:
import sys


def fast_power(base, e):
    if e == 0:
        return 1
    half = fast_power(base, e // 2)
    if e % 2 == 0:
        return half * half
    return half * half * base


def main():
    sys.setrecursionlimit(100000)

    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    base = int(data[0])
    e = int(data[1])
    print(fast_power(base, e))


main()

questions.title: Count Subsets With Sum S
questions.description:
A promo engine counts how many selections of the sampled products add up to exactly S. Each product may be taken at most once; the counter walks the list recursively (take it or leave it).

The program scaffolding (input reading and main) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def count_subsets(values, target):

Return the number of subsets of values (including the empty subset) whose elements sum to target, using RECURSIVE include/exclude calls on the rest of the list. Loops and itertools are banned — the grader rejects for, while and itertools.

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of values.
Line 2: n integers.
Line 3: the target sum.

Output Format:
One line with the number of subsets summing to target.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10
-50 <= value <= 50
0 <= target <= 200
questions.sourcecode:
import sys


def count_subsets(values, target):
    if not values:
        return 1 if target == 0 else 0
    head = values[0]
    rest = values[1:]
    return count_subsets(rest, target) + count_subsets(rest, target - head)


def main():
    sys.setrecursionlimit(100000)

    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    values = list(map(int, data[1:1 + n]))
    target = int(data[1 + n])
    print(count_subsets(values, target))


main()

questions.title: Distinct Letter Arrangements
questions.description:
A gift-shop sign maker wants to know how many DISTINCT layouts its letter tiles can form (duplicate letters collapse into one layout). Count them by recursive backtracking over the tile positions.

The program scaffolding (input reading and main) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def count_arrangements(letters):

Return the number of distinct arrangements of the letters (an empty word has exactly 1 arrangement). Recursion with itertools is banned — the grader rejects itertools.

Input Format:
Line 1: the word (lowercase letters).

Output Format:
One line with the number of distinct arrangements.

Constraints:
1 <= len(letters) <= 7
questions.sourcecode:
import sys


def count_arrangements(letters):
    if not letters:
        return 1
    seen = []
    total = 0
    i = 0
    while i < len(letters):
        ch = letters[i]
        if ch not in seen:
            seen.append(ch)
            rest = letters[:i] + letters[i + 1:]
            total += count_arrangements(rest)
        i += 1
    return total


def main():
    sys.setrecursionlimit(100000)

    letters = sys.stdin.read().split()[0]
    print(count_arrangements(letters))


main()

questions.title: Count Digit Occurrences Recursively
questions.description:
A device logger counts how many times a given digit appears in a device id — using arithmetic recursion (peel the last digit with % 10 and // 10), never string conversion.

The program scaffolding (input reading and main) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def count_digit(n, d):

Return how many times digit d occurs in the decimal representation of n, computed RECURSIVELY on n // 10. String conversion is banned — the grader rejects str(.

Input Format:
Line 1: the non-negative integer n.
Line 2: the digit d (0-9).

Output Format:
One line with the number of occurrences of d in n.

Constraints:
0 <= n <= 2000000000
0 <= d <= 9
questions.sourcecode:
import sys


def count_digit(n, d):
    if n < 10:
        return 1 if n == d else 0
    rest = count_digit(n // 10, d)
    if n % 10 == d:
        return rest + 1
    return rest


def main():
    sys.setrecursionlimit(100000)

    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    d = int(data[1])
    print(count_digit(n, d))


main()

questions.title: Every Product Bundle
questions.description:
The promo engine must list every possible non-empty bundle of the n sampled products before printing the promo cards. Generate the bundles by recursion (take the first product or skip it).

The program scaffolding (input reading and main) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def all_subsets(values):

Return a list of tuples — every non-empty subset of values. The hidden harness sorts the tuples and prints one bundle per line, so the order you return them in does not matter. itertools is banned — the grader rejects itertools.

Input Format:
Line 1: n, the number of sampled products.

questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= n <= 5; 1 <= value <= 50; values distinct and ascending
questions.sourcecode:
import sys


def all_subsets(values):
    if not values:
        return []
    rest = all_subsets(values[1:])
    return rest + [(values[0],)] + [(values[0],) + s for s in rest]


def main():
    sys.setrecursionlimit(100000)

    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    values = list(map(int, data[1:1 + n]))
    subs = all_subsets(values)
    subs.sort()
    lines = []
    for s in subs:
        lines.append(' '.join(map(str, s)))
    print('\n'.join(lines))


main()

questions.title: Nth Lexicographic Permutation
questions.description:
A cipher wheel needs the k-th arrangement of its letter ring in dictionary order. With the letters given ascending, the block-size trick picks one letter per call and recurses on the remainder.

The program scaffolding (input reading and main) is already set up for you. Implement only this function:

    def nth_permutation(letters, k):

letters holds DISTINCT lowercase letters in ascending order and k is 1-based with 1 <= k <= len(letters)!. Return the k-th permutation in lexicographic order. Recursively: block = factorial(len(letters) - 1) (write a recursive helper — itertools is banned); idx = (k - 1) // block; answer = letters[idx] + nth_permutation(rest, k - idx * block) where rest is letters without position idx.

Input Format:
Line 1: the letters (distinct, ascending).
Line 2: the rank k.

Output Format:
One line with the k-th lexicographic permutation.

Constraints:
1 <= len(letters) <= 6
1 <= k <= len(letters)!
questions.inputconstrains: 1 <= len(letters) <= 6; letters distinct and ascending; 1 <= k <= len(letters)!
